summary: This Advent sermon explores hope as the first of four Advent themes, using the metaphor of sheep walking in circles to illustrate how people remain trapped in patterns of sin and anxiety despite Christ offering freedom. The preacher emphasizes that Jesus' incarnation was an 'ignition event' that broke the circle, offering hope in three dimensions: immediate deliverance (justification), ongoing transformation (sanctification), and ultimate restoration (glorification).
key_points: Advent anticipates both Christ's first coming and His return
Jesus stepped into our confining circles of sin to lead us out into freedom
The 'great exchange': Christ became sin so we could become righteous
Biblical hope has three fulfillments—immediate (justification), in-life (sanctification), and eternal (glorification)
God promises deliverance now, transformation in this life, and complete restoration at Christ's return
big_idea: Jesus came to break us out of the confining circles of sin and offers hope for immediate deliverance, ongoing transformation in this life, and ultimate restoration when He returns.
title: Born: HOPE
